title: Utility of the continuous spectrum formed by pathological states in characterizing disease properties.
authors: Fujiwara, Takashi; Kariya, Yoshiaki; Kobayashi, Kanata; Matsui, Soma; Takada, Tappei
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习从疾病转录组连续谱中识别转录因子，但核心是疾病状态表征而非TF-DNA结合互作建模，仅间接涉及转录因子，无蛋白-DNA互作机制或AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Understanding diseases as the result of continuous transitions from a healthy system is more realistic than understanding them as discrete states. Here, we designed the spectrum formation approach (SFA), a machine learning-based method that extracts key features contributing to disease state continuity. We applied the SFA to transcriptomic data from patients with progressive liver disease and neurodegenerative movement disorders to examine its effectiveness in identifying biologically relevant gene sets. The SFA identified transcription factors that potentially regulate liver inflammation and voluntary movement. In neurodegenerative disorders, the SFA also identified genes regulated by ETS-1, with unclear effects on movement. In functional assessment using human iPSC-derived neurons, ETS-1 overexpression disrupted dopamine receptor balance, reduced GABA-producing enzyme levels, and promoted cell death. These findings suggest that the SFA enables the discovery of regulatory factors capable of modifying disease states and provides a framework for the continuity-based interpretation of biological systems.
abstract_zh: 将疾病理解为从健康系统连续转变的结果，比将其视为离散状态更为现实。在此，我们设计了谱系形成方法（SFA），这是一种基于机器学习的方法，用于提取促成疾病状态连续性的关键特征。我们将SFA应用于进行性肝病和神经退行性运动障碍患者的转录组数据，以检验其在识别生物学相关基因集方面的有效性。SFA识别出可能调节肝脏炎症和自主运动的转录因子。在神经退行性疾病中，SFA还识别出受ETS-1调控的基因，其对运动的影响尚不明确。在使用人诱导多能干细胞来源的神经元进行的功能评估中，ETS-1过表达破坏了多巴胺受体平衡，减少了GABA合成酶水平，并促进了细胞死亡。这些发现表明，SFA能够发现可改变疾病状态的调控因子，并为基于连续性的生物系统解释提供了框架。
